title: Change a dressing with one clean hand and one dirty hand
instruction: Use only the right gripper for the stained used dressing and only the left gripper for the white clean pad, and keep the right gripper away from the clean pad. Put the used dressing in the yellow waste bin, then put the clean pad on the pink wound mark. Apart from the left gripper, the clean pad may touch only its blue tray and the wound mark, and it must never pass over or under the used dressing.
context: Dressing changes by nurses and home health aides (O*NET 29-1141 Registered Nurses, 29-2061 Licensed Practical Nurses, 31-1121 Home Health Aides) often use a 'clean hand / dirty hand' (non-touch) technique: one hand handles only the soiled dressing and the other only the sterile supplies, so a contaminated glove never touches the sterile pad; the soiled dressing goes into the waste bin before the new pad comes over the wound, nothing soiled passes over anything sterile, and the sterile pad touches nothing but its tray and the wound. As at a bedside, the sterile tray is on the clean hand's side and the waste bin on the dirty hand's side, so each arm reaches only its own end of the job, but both reach the wound, where the roles must be kept: which gripper goes near which item is checked at every moment, not only at the end. Unlike a plain swap, the hand discipline along the way is scored.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five things are on the table. (1) Wound mark: a flat pink silicone pad standing in for the skin round a wound, 70 x 70 mm and 2 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0, sides parallel to x and y. (2) Used dressing: a loose absorbent gauze pad stained yellow-brown, 50 x 50 x 16 mm, 20 g (it holds exudate), lying flat and centred on the wound mark, sides parallel to x and y. (3) Sterile tray: a blue rigid plastic tray, four walls 6 mm thick and 15 mm tall round a 140 x 70 mm floor (140 mm along x), fixed to the table, centred at x 24.0 cm, y +22.0 cm; in simulation the table top is its floor. (4) Clean pad: a loose white sterile gauze pad, 50 x 50 x 16 mm, 10 g (dry and tightly folded), lying flat and centred in the tray, sides parallel to x and y. (5) Waste bin: a yellow rigid plastic clinical waste bin, four walls 8 mm thick and 40 mm tall round a 90 x 90 mm floor, fixed to the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y -24.0 cm; in simulation the table top is its floor. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads both pads and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). It cannot see a gripper's heading, so each gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within a radius of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper, the radius reaching a finger's outer corner (half the current finger gap plus the 8 mm finger thickness, and half the fingers' 27 mm width across; 57 mm fully open). Outlines (seen from above) and distances between objects use world-aligned bounding boxes. Rules: (1) the left gripper's finger zone comes within 5 mm of the used dressing; (2) the right gripper's finger zone comes within 30 mm of the clean pad; (3) the clean pad and the used dressing come within 3 mm of each other, or their outlines overlap at any height (one carried over the other); (4) the clean pad's outline overlaps the wound mark's while the used dressing is not yet in the bin; (5) a corner of the clean pad is less than 1 mm above the table top, or below it, at a point over neither the tray's floor (within 2 mm of its walls) nor the wound mark; (6) the clean pad comes within 3 mm of the bin. 'In the bin' means the used dressing's centre is over the bin's 90 x 90 mm floor and below its rim. 'Flat on the wound mark' means the clean pad is tilted less than 5 degrees (either 50 x 50 mm face down), its lowest point is within 3 mm of the mark's top, and its centre is within the stated distance of the mark's centre horizontally. A gripper has 'let go' of its item (the left the clean pad, the right the used dressing) when its opening is 0.9 or more (fingers at least 84.5 mm apart) or its finger zone is more than 10 mm from that item. Score 0 if any rule is broken at any moment, whatever happens afterwards, or if the used dressing ends off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise: 1.0 if the used dressing is in the bin and the clean pad is flat on the wound mark within 10 mm, with both grippers let go; 0.75 if the used dressing is in the bin and the clean pad is flat on the mark within 25 mm, but further off than 10 mm or with a gripper not let go; 0.5 if the used dressing is in the bin; 0.25 if the used dressing is off the wound mark (no part of its outline over the mark) but not in the bin; 0 in every other case (the used dressing still on the wound mark). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with both pads still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, rules 1 and 2 are not applied and 'both grippers let go' is taken as met. In a real trial, rules 1 to 6 are judged frame by frame from top and side video, with a 30 mm scale bar on the tray's rim.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, all with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The wound mark, tray and bin are fixed; both pads are uniform-density rigid boxes of the stated sizes and masses (real gauze is soft and conforms to the skin). Sterility is not simulated: the clean/dirty rules check the fingers and pads, not the rest of each arm. Gripper heading is not read, so each finger zone is round, wider than the real fingers across their closing direction.
reset_notes: Put the used dressing back flat and centred on the wound mark and the clean pad back flat and centred in the tray, sides parallel to x and y. A real build uses a fresh stained pad and a fresh clean pad for each trial; nothing else is consumed.
